title_original: AWS Trainium Frontier competition: Co-design models and kernels on purpose-built AI chips
description: A competition with a finalist ceremony during NeurIPS 2026, challenging researchers to train language models from scratch on Trainium, exploring what optimal architectures look like when the hardware changes.
title_he: AWS Trainium Frontier competition: Co-design models and kernels on purpose-built AI chips
summary_he: בתחרות AWS Trainium Frontier, מדענים מחפשים את הארכיטקטורה האופטימלית של דגמי לשון, כשהם משתמשים במעבדי AI ייעודיים.
details_he: התחרות, שהתקיימה במסגרת NeurIPS 2026, כללה שתי שלבים: שלב ראשון של 30 דקות על מעבד Trainium2, ושלב שני של 4 שעות על שרת מלא, עם דגימות נבחרות. המנצחים קיבלו הכרה במסגרת NeurIPS, הזדמנויות לפרסום משותף עם מדענים מ-AWS, ופרסי כסף. התחרות הייתה חלק מניסיון להבין את הארכיטקטורה האופטימלית של דגמי לשון, כשהם משתמשים במעבדי AI ייעודיים. המעבדים הייעודיים, כמו AWS Trainium, מציעים פני שטח תכנותיים שונים, עם זיכרון SRAM, שליטה ישירה בתנועת הנתונים, ומעבדים סיסטוליים. התחרות נועדה לחקור את הארכיטקטורה האופטימלית של דגמי לשון, כשהם משתמשים במעבדי AI ייעודיים.

title_original: The Permanent Threat: Analyzing Aeternum’s Blockchain-Based C2 Operations and Communications
description: Analysis of the Aeternum botnet loader, a threat leveraging Polygon blockchain smart contracts for decentralized C2 infrastructure and payload execution.The postThe Permanent Threat: Analyzing Aeternum’s Blockchain-Based C2 Operations and Communicationsappeared first onUnit 42.
title_he: The Permanent Threat: Analyzing Aeternum’s Blockchain-Based C2 Operations and Communications
summary_he: Aeternum, a C++ botnet loader, has been discovered to use the Polygon blockchain for command-and-control operations, making it a highly resilient and low-cost threat. This shift to blockchain-based operations complicates existing law enforcement takedown methods. The Aeternum botnet uses various evasion techniques to operate effectively.
details_he: Aeternum's use of the Polygon blockchain for C2 operations allows threat actors to write encrypted and plaintext instructions directly using smart contracts. Infected devices continuously query public RPC endpoints to retrieve and execute these on-chain commands. The Aeternum botnet also employs decentralized networks and evasion techniques, such as virtual machine detection and antivirus scanning, to evade detection. This combination of factors makes Aeternum a highly resilient and low-cost threat that complicates existing law enforcement takedown methods. Palo Alto Networks customers are better protected from the threats discussed in this article through various products and services, including Advanced WildFire, Advanced URL Filtering, and Advanced DNS Security.

title_original: Native AI Security Comes to Claude: Why Anthropic’s Inference Hooks Matter
description: Anthropic’s new inference hooks give enterprises a native enforcement point before prompts ever reach the model. Combined with Check Point Workforce AI Security, organizations get a real-time allow-or-deny decision on every prompt, with no proxy in the path. Why This Matters Enterprise AI adoption has moved well past experimentation. Employees draft documents, write code, summarize meetings, and query enterprise knowledge through large language models every day. The challenge was never understanding that AI introduces risk. It was finding a practical enforcement point. Web gateways and Data Loss Prevention (DLP) tools were designed for websites and SaaS applications, not conversations with […]The postNative AI Security Comes to Claude: Why Anthropic’s Inference Hooks Matterappeared first onCheck Point Blog.
title_he: Native AI Security Comes to Claude: Why Anthropic’s Inference Hooks Matter
summary_he: Anthropic's new inference hooks for Claude Enterprise allow organizations to enforce security decisions in real-time, without the need for proxies or additional infrastructure. This integration with Check Point Workforce AI Security provides a unified policy set for all AI tools, ensuring that every prompt and tool call is evaluated against existing DLP and attack protection rules.
details_he: The challenge of securing AI adoption in enterprises has been finding a practical enforcement point. Traditional security tools, such as web gateways and Data Loss Prevention (DLP) tools, were designed for websites and SaaS applications, not conversations with AI models. Anthropic's inference hooks change this by providing a native enforcement point before prompts ever reach the model. This allows organizations to evaluate every prompt and tool call in real-time, making it easier to enforce security decisions and prevent potential risks. The integration with Check Point Workforce AI Security provides a seamless and efficient way to implement this security feature, with no need for additional infrastructure or proxies.
